properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: hash.js@1.1.7 (SHA-1/SHA-2 family) declared in the bitcoin example project's lockfile, transitively via elliptic. Dependency inventory: the library ships SHA-1 among its digests with the build; no direct hash.js call site exists in bitcoin/bitcoinjs-lib/src (the wallet code hashes through bip39/bip32/bitcoinjs-lib instead). Same package as LIB-e966a74e.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js@4.2.0 is a declared dependency of the blockchain TypeScript demo project (used for SHA-256 block hashing in src/ch*). The package ships MD5 in its shipped library surface; no MD5 call site found in the application source. Changeable here by dropping/upgrading the dependency.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: crypto-js@4.2.0 declared dependency of the blockchain demo project; SHA-1 is available in the shipped library (legacy algorithms) though the app's own hashing uses SHA-256. Changeable here by dependency choice.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA over secp256k1 is the signature curve of the Bitcoin and Ethereum protocols — bitcoinjs-lib, the ethereum noah-token contracts and the solana app all declare secp256k1 implementations in their dependency trees. The algorithm is fixed by the blockchain platforms themselves, so it is changeable only through protocol evolution (Bitcoin/Ethereum ecosystem); for this codebase the posture note is: every transaction signature made by these stacks is quantum-unsafe (Shor). Migration target ML-DSA-

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: evp_bytestokey is a transitive dependency (via browserify-AES/crypto-browserify stack in the web3 toolchain) in the bitcoin, ethereum and solana JS projects. Single-round-MD5 KDF is available in the shipped tree; no direct application call site. Changeable only through the upstream dependency chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Poly1305 MAC machinery in the ethereum/frontend and solana/solana-pyth-price-feeds/app dependency trees (web3/NextAuth stack). Ships with both Next.js builds; no direct Poly1305 call site found in the frontend's own pages/api code.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: isChainValid() in a naive blockchain tutorial re-verifies every block hash with !== instead of a constant-time compare. Exploitability is minimal (verdict is also observable from the return value), but the pattern is real and this is the project's own integrity check — a posture control worth recording. Changeable here.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: bcrypt-pbkdf (bcrypt-based PBKDF used for OpenSSH/sshpk key stretching) is a declared dependency in the noah-token truffle/hardhat stack. KDF available in shipped tree; no application call site. Changeable through dependency selection.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Weak randomness in IPFS pin display names for NFT uploads. Note the template interpolates ${Math.random} WITHOUT parentheses — it interpolates the function object's source string ("function random() { [native code] }"), so the "random" suffix is in fact constant across calls. Low direct security impact (Pinata metadata name; the IPFS CID is the real content identifier), but a genuine non-cryptographic-randomness use in an upload endpoint.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: node-forge@1.3.1 ships RSA (keygen, sign, encrypt) and TLS utilities. Declared dependency of the solana pyth price-feeds Next.js app (likely via selfsigned/webpack dev-server chain). RSA available in shipped library; no application RSA call site found. Changeable here via dependency choice.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: @noble/curves@1.4.0 in the solana app lockfile includes ECDSA over secp256k1 among its curve implementations. Same logical asset as ALG-673c8f24 (secp256k1 availability) reached through a different package; @noble/curves also ships P-256 and Ed25519 (separate objects). Available in shipped library; no direct application call site found.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 signature primitives in the two Next.js apps' dependency trees (@noble/ed25519 via the noble stack, @stablelib/ed25519 via the stablelib stack). Available to any code in those builds; quantum-vulnerable signature primitive with a scheduled migration (ML-DSA).

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: create-ecdh is the crypto-browserify ECDH shim (elliptic-curve Diffie-Hellman over secp256k1/curve25519 etc.), declared in the noah-token and solana app JS trees (transitive via crypto-browserify) and present in the bitcoin lockfile. Quantum-unsafe key agreement available in the shipped libraries; no application call site found. Changeable via the browserify shim chain.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: X25519 key agreement available in the two Next.js apps' dependency trees (stablelib stack, pulled in by the web3/auth dependency graph). Harvest-now-decrypt-later relevant if used for session/ECDH purposes by dependencies.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@1.0.3 ships Ed25519 signatures. Declared in the noah-token (ethereum contract tooling) and solana app lockfiles, likely via sshpk/ssh-style deps. Ed25519 is quantum-unsafe (Shor) though a strong classical choice; available in shipped library, no application call site found in these directories.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA/secp256k1 library available to the bitcoin example build. The project's own scripts sign via the tiny-secp256k1/ECPair/bitcoinjs-message wrappers (see the live findings), but elliptic ships in the lockfile regardless. Same package as LIB-a0bfbc1a.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Curve25519 arithmetic behind Ed25519 verification in the Solana program's dependency stack. The program source (src/lib.rs, 199 lines) makes no direct crypto calls — its security model rides on Solana runtime Ed25519 transaction signatures via Signer account constraints, which is exactly what this crate supports. Same package as LIB-f69df116.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: P-256 (secp256r1) ECDSA availability via @noble/curves@1.4.0 in the solana app lockfile. Quantum-unsafe (Shor); no application call site found in the app source. Changeable here via dependency choice.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: tweetnacl@1.0.3 ships X25519 scalar multiplication (crypto_box key agreement). Declared in the noah-token lockfile; X25519 is quantum-unsafe (Shor breaks ECDH). Available in shipped library, no application call site found in this directory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: One logical asset: Keccak-256 (the Ethereum ecosystem hash, preimage-strength only Grover-affected). (a) keccak256 builtin in the compiled contracts' Yul/ABI — the hash the deployed NoahNFT/NoahToken/Airdrop/Faucet bytecode actually uses; (b) @ethersproject/keccak256 and keccak npm packages in the ethereum/contract, noah-token, frontend and solana-app lockfiles — what ethers uses for address checksums and event-topic hashing.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: PBKDF2 KDF available in the shipped trees: the standalone pbkdf2 npm package, @types/pbkdf2, @ethersproject/pbkdf2 ^5.7.0 (ethers.js BIP39 mnemonic-to-seed path) in the ethereum contract tooling, pbkdf2 ^3.0.3/^3.1.2 in the solana app, and the pbkdf2 crate in the solana Rust program's Cargo.lock. KDF available in shipped libraries; iteration counts are decided by callers (ethers uses 2048 for BIP39, NIST minimum 1000). Changeable via dependency choice.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: scrypt-js (the scrypt memory-hard KDF used by ethers.js for BIP39 mnemonic-to-seed derivation, N=131072) is declared throughout the ethereum tooling: noah-token, ethereum/contract root and ethereum/frontend lockfiles. Strong password KDF, quantum-safe in the Grover sense; available in shipped library, no application call site found. Changeable via dependency choice.
